c89da9a40bdfc0ff9f01bb624c8cdf92.text: Kendal and Geoff Bourdon with Woodland Jewellers hope to raise $12,000 this year through their annual raffle supporting the Cariboo Memorial Hospital Foundation. The 18-karat yellow gold valued at $9,900 features a teal sapphire accented with champagne diamonds. Geoff Bourdon likes pushing himself every year with designing and handcrafting a one-of-a-kind piece of jewellery raising funds for the Cariboo Memorial Hospital Foundation. Since 2009 the fourth generation owner of Woodland Jewellers has annually designed an exquisite raffle prize that has now raised $190,000 for the not-for-profit to purchase medical equipment for the Cariboo Memorial Hospital. This year’s prize is an 18-karat yellow gold ring featuring a teal sapphire accented with champagne diamonds. It is valued at $9,900. “If we sell out the tickets we’re going to break over the $200,000 mark for fundraisers,” said Woodland Jewellers manager and bookkeeper, Kendal Bourdon, who is also Geoff’s wife. About 30 hours of fabrication to make the ring was spent by Geoff who also mixed the 18-karat gold. He spent months, however, in advance on the design process. “I normally always start with the gemstone,” Geoff said, adding he believes his work should always complement the gemstone that is the centre of the piece. “If there’s a gemstone that I really want to work with then the design comes from the gemstone. Even this year the shape of the ring is a reflection of the cut of the gemstone, and the colours having the fancy natural round diamonds in the yellow gold brings out a lot of the green and the teal in the sapphire.” Each piece of jewellery he has presented in the annual raffle prize since 2009 is unique with Geoff pushing himself each year to do something he has either not technically or in style done before. 858097a3f7c147321b4972d61a6de839.text: The Quesnel River Rush played with the Quesnel Millionaires' jersey for Retro Night. **Thursday, Oct. 29 – Quesnel River Rush 3, Williams Lake Mustangs 11** The Quesnel River Rush watched a promising start unravel Thursday night as the Williams Lake Mustangs scored 10 goals over the final two periods in an 11-3 rout at the West Fraser Centre. On Thursday, Oct. 29, the River Rush opened the scoring exchanges with a strong start, keeping pace with Williams Lake through the first period. The Mustangs struck first when Kaelen Swanson scored at 2:31, but Quesnel responded just 26 seconds later as Luke Van Imschoot buried his ninth goal of the season on the power play at 2:57. The teams headed into the first intermission tied 1-1, with Quesnel showing early signs of being able to match the visiting Mustangs. Quesnel carried that momentum into the second period when Austin Root scored his first goal of the season at 3:24 to give the River Rush a 2-1 lead. However, Williams Lake quickly turned the game around. Kaden Charpentier tied the contest on the power play at 10:14 before Swanson scored twice in just over two minutes, including a power-play marker, to put the Mustangs ahead 4-2. Tristan Aidoo added another at 14:53, sending Williams Lake into the second intermission with a 5-2 advantage. The Mustangs continued to build their lead in the third period, with Logan Hauk scoring at 1:33. Quesnel’s Jimmy Proulx answered at 3:30 with his first goal of the season, briefly cutting into the deficit and making it 6-3. Williams Lake responded with five unanswered goals to close out the game. Braden Bolt scored at 4:30, followed by power-play goals from Chaz Lucas, Declan Pocock, Carter Krueger and Matthew Hufty as the Mustangs pulled away for the 11-3 victory. The Mustangs also controlled the shot count, outshooting Quesnel 54-31. Williams Lake recorded 28 shots in the third period alone, compared to just six for the River Rush. d5265745c8cb5b8b026c6b8d5c5407bd.text: Members of the Royal Canadian Air Force are able to training in aircraft maintenance engineering thanks to a new partnership with Okanagan College. Okanagan College’s Aircraft Maintenance Engineering is helping bolster Canada’s military and defence. Twenty-two members of the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) joined the college program in October. An agreement was signed by the two organizations to have RCAF members train at the Kelowna and Vernon airports. “This collaboration between the Royal Canadian Air Force and Okanagan College demonstrates how Canada’s government is protecting Canadians by forging new partnerships to strengthen our sovereignty and national security,” said Stephen Fuhr, Member of Parliament for Kelowna and Secretary of State for Defence Procurement. “This partnership is about diversifying training opportunities for new aircraft technicians at a time of growth for the RCAF,” said Brigadier-General Dan Coutts, Commander of 2 Canadian Air Division which is responsible for RCAF training. “This initiative is representative of the Defence Industrial Strategy, partnering with industry and academia to train technicians that will maintain the sophisticated aircraft of Canada’s Air Force today and into the future.” RCAF members will live in the college’s campus housing in Vernon during training. “We’re excited to be able to work in partnership with the Royal Canadian Air Force, helping to support their workforce demands and the efforts of the Canadian military, alongside our civilian cohorts of students,” said Caitlin Hartigan, Dean of Trades and Apprenticeship at Okanagan College. “There is significant demand for Aircraft Maintenance Engineers, and our program is focused on being agile and responsive in order to continue to produce skilled workers for the region and beyond.” The course is open to all students at Okanagan College with two aircraft maintenance programs, structures and mechanical.

f67b019fd01f8463699750f014a51983.text: A South Cariboo man has been arrested for several charges, including committing violence towards an intimate partner. On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the 100 Mile House RCMP and the Cariboo Crime Reduction Unit executed a search warrant at a residence located along the 5400-block of Canim Hendrix Lake Road. The warrant was executed in relation to allegations of threats. They were supported by the North District Emergency Response Team. Cpl. Jennifer Cooper said that during this operation, a man associated with the residence was located and arrested a short distance from the home. Cooper identified him as 36-year-old Dylan Ryder Gropp. Gropp has been charged with the following four offences: conspiracy to commit an indictable offence; uttering threats to burn, destroy or damage; criminal harassment and committing a violent offence against an intimate partner. None of these charges has been proven in a court of law. Cooper said that Gropp will remain in custody until his next court date.

A new precedent has been set for drought codes in British Columbia. At the Canadian Wildfire Conference, held at the KF Centre for Excellence in Kelowna on Oct. 28-29, B.C. Wildfire Service (BCWS) Provincial Aviation Specialist J.J. Lum provided a summary of the season. The French Bar weather station, the one nearest the Big Bar Complex, recorded drought levels above the 100th percentile of the 30-year average between May and mid-August. Weather stations nearest the Brunswick Complex and the Bald Range wildfire also recorded above the 100th percentile through August. “We were facing drought like we’ve never seen before,” Lum said, noting that the Bald Range wildfire sparked around the same time the drought code peaked in Penticton. Between Apr. 1 and Oct. 1, B.C. saw over 1,400 new fire starts and 10 wildfires of note, affecting more than 53,000 British Columbians across 53 communities and First Nations, and burning over 477,000 hectares. “The Cariboo Fire Centre, they were the big winner or the big loser depending on how you look at it, with 233 wildfires resulting in over 200,000 hectares burned,” Lum said. “To note, they are also the smallest fire centre.” The north saw a calmer season than normal, with the Northwest and Prince George centres combined seeing 218 wildfires burn 1,349 hectares. B.C.’s fire season was average for the number of fires, Lum said. “But really it’s not the number of wildfires you have, it’s where they start and how big they get.” Throughout the summer, BCWS deployed 1,863 personnel, engaged with 126 fire departments. The crews were also supported by fire personnel from across the globe, including multiple Canadian provinces and territories, Parks Canada, Canadian Forest Service, Mexico, Costa Rica, Australia and New Zealand. 5490cbc14230f5e4d8ed6ca2955867d8.text: Obama-backed doc film focused on Ghana produced by woman with B.C. roots | Williams Lake Tribune Obama-backed doc film focused on Ghana produced by woman with B.C. roots A scene from The Eyes of Ghana, a documentary film released in October 2026. Surrey-raised filmmaker Nana Adwoa Frimpong produced *The Eyes of Ghana*, an acclaimed documentary executive-produced by U.S. presidential couple Barack and Michelle Obama, Higher Ground founders. The 90-minute feature doc explores the life and work of 93-year-old Ghanaian filmmaker Chris Hesse, whose archive chronicles Ghana’s early years as a sovereign nation. Hesse served as personal cameraman to Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first president. As his eyesight faded, Hesse rescued more than 1,000 films capturing the West Africa country’s fight for independence in the 1950s and 60s. The film, world-premiered a year ago at Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), is now in theatres across North America including Surrey’s Landmark Guildford on Sunday, Nov. 1. Frimpong, a director, writer and creative producer, says she’s thrilled to have the movie shown in her hometown. “My parents still live there (in Surrey) and they’re inviting everybody they know,” Frimpong said on the phone from New York City. “It’s exciting. I never dreamed that my home theatre would play a film that I produced. It’s very cool.” A Surrey resident until age 18, Frimpong now lives in Los Angeles and works for Breakwater Studios to “illuminate stories of women and people of colour,” the company website notes. Frimpong’s parents grew up in Ghana and later found a home in Canada with their children. “For me to be making a film like this, my first big film, and to have it call back to where my parents are from, where my sisters and I grew up knowing and believing was an extension of our home (in Canada), it’s a dream come true.” Frimpong’s passion for storytelling, the Breakwater website says, is marked by her past community organizing work around accessibility

c3cc61b38e0e49365baca20347503cab.text: Halloween festivities will once again be available in downtown Williams Lake. Jazmyn Douillard with The Realm of Toys & The Nerd Room is extra happy for this year’s Downtown Trick r Treat in downtown Williams Lake. With Halloween falling on a Saturday, it was initially unclear if the annual festivities would be a go as many businesses, including professional services and government agencies, are closed on weekends. As it appeared there would be less than half the number of businesses participating from last year consideration was given to cancelling. Luckily for trick-or-treaters the decision was made to forge ahead with a total of 22 businesses, some only available for an hour or two, signing up to hand out candy and other treats. For years Douillard has organized the Downtown Trick r Treat annual festivities with her mother, Joan. She personally likes the 2 p.m. start time which is quiet, providing the perfect opportunity for toddlers, kids with sensory or sensitivity issues and anyone who might get overwhelmed to trick-or-treat before things pick up. She remembers the first Downtown Trick r Treat with about 15 locations signed up and running to Safeway to buy whatever she could to drop off after they ran out of candy in just 15 minutes. The biggest year for handing out candy at the Realm of Toys was before COVID with 744 kids. “After COVID we definitely saw a huge drop in numbers and it’s only slowly been increasing,” Douillard said, adding last year they hit over 500. This year they’re making sure they have enough for 650, and have spent between $600 to $800 to ensure costumed kids receive a mix of candy and even a comic or child’s book and possibly small seasonal toys, averaging about $1.25 per trick-or-treater. 1deca6730a0ff1a190da8242fcbdabcc.text: The City of Victoria has issued a safety warning after an owl attacked the same person twice in three days. On Oct. 4, bylaw staff received a complaint about a barred owl attacking a resident on the shared pedestrian and bike walkway along Dallas Road, between Douglas Road and the Beacon Hill Park Road exit. Signage was subsequently installed to raise awareness for park users regarding an “aggressive” barred owl in the area. “This activity is common and is typically a result of territory enforcement as adult owls look to establish new or protect existing territories,” the city said in a statement. This is the first time signage in Victoria has been installed to increase awareness for park users about owl attacks. Parks staff continue to monitor the situation and will remove the signage once the activity subsides. Ann Nightingale, a Rocky Point Bird Observatory volunteer, told Black Press in 2025 that territorial behaviour stems from the birds’ instinct to protect their young. Other times, however, owls attack people in the hopes of snagging a quick meal. “Sometimes … they mistake the movement of a ponytail or pompom as a prey item,” she said. “They primarily hunt by sound, so the swishing of hair on a jacket can sound like a small animal moving.” Nightingale recommended avoiding areas where attacks have recently occurred. “The owls that do this tend to be repeat offenders,” she said. “Once you know where they are, just give them a bit of space. They are usually defending a specific territory. If you need to walk that path, an open umbrella should keep the bird away or at least provide a barrier.” People with small cats and dogs are also advised to be cautious as owls can see them as prey. (Image Credit: Andy Devlin/Edmonton Oil Kings) EDMONTON — There were no Halloween scaries for Vit Zahejsky and the Kamloops Blazers at Rogers Place in Edmonton, as they skated to a 4-1 victory over the Edmonton Oil Kings on Saturday (Oct. 31) afternoon. The win also moved Blazers head coach Shaun Clouston into sole possession of fourth place on the Western Hockey League’s all-time wins leaderboard. Clouston picked up win number 627 to move past longtime WHL head coach Lorne Molleken. Zahejsky’s seventh goal of the season came via a shorthanded penalty shot at 13:51 of the first period as the Blazers took a 1-0 lead. Ty Bonkowski doubled the lead early in the second, but Edmonton pulled one back at 11:58 through Kayden Stroeder. He scored on a five-minute powerplay after Blazers defenceman Madden Tymchak was assessed a boarding major and game misconduct, but the Oil Kings weren’t able to beat Kaeden Tate a second time. Tate turned aside 20 of 21 shots to improve to 6-1 this season, with a 1.96 goals against average and a .937 save percentage. Logan Lanti scored his first of the season to make it 3-1 Kamloops early in the third period before Mikhail Cherepanov’s empty netter at 18:45 sealed the win for the visitors. Oil Kings netminder Parker Snell stopped 27 of 30 shots in a losing effort, as Edmonton dropped to 6-5-1-0 on the season. The Blazers moved to 8-4-2-0, to sit second in the B.C. Division and third in the Western Conference The Blazers head to Calgary next to face the 8-6-0-0 Hitmen in a Sunday (Nov. 1) matinee at Scotiabank Saddledome. Puck drop is set for 2:00 p.m. Alberta time. They’ll also play the Red Deer Rebels on Tuesday (Nov. 3) before returning home to host the Seattle Thunderbirds at Sandman Centre on Friday (Nov. 6). Kaden Charpentier and Landon Gillanders earned first and second star honour, respectively, in the Williams Lake Mustang's win over the Summerland Jets on Friday, Oct. 30. Brayden Bolt and Ivan Anderson earned first and second star honours respectively, in the Williams Lake Mustang's 4-3 shootout win over the Fernie Ghostriders on Halloween night. The Williams Lake Mustangs kept their winning streak alive over Halloween weekend, following a 4-2 victory over the Summerland Jets and a 4-3 shootout win against the Fernie Ghostriders on Saturday night. During the Mustangs’ game against the Summerland Jets, a three-goal second period was the key to winning. Summerland fired first, scoring the lone goal of the opening period, before Braden Bolt drew Williams Lake level in the second. 0355238bcad7c3aa6f274eb24ff93679.text: Helping coach the Williams Lake Minor Hockey Association's World Girls’ Ice Hockey Weekend at the Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex was Terry Duff. Girls U15 Rep Team coach Terry Duff was on the ice on Oct. 31 helping out with World Girls’ Ice Hockey Weekend. “Hockey is for everybody,” Terry Duff recently told a group of young female hockey players in Williams Lake, encouraging them to believe in themselves, work hard and always try their best. “Girls can do anything anyone can do.” Duff’s words of empowerment came after more than 40 girls from U7 through U15 hit the ice on Saturday, Oct. 31 at the Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex to celebrate World Girls’ Ice Hockey Weekend. According to Hockey Canada, the International Ice Hockey Federation has united countries around the world since 2011 for World Girls’ Ice Hockey Weekend events aimed to retain, recruit and engage players, coaches, officials and fans of all ages. In Williams Lake Duff was one of the coaches helping lead the day that included a number of drills, activities and games. “We have a big increase in girls hockey, and hopefully with somebody like myself who is really advocating to get the girls on the ice and have all these ice times the numbers will increase even more,” said Williams Lake Minor Hockey Association female coordinator Courtney Petryshen, noting the girls U18 Rep Team could not make the day being away in Prince George for weekend games. Among the parents in the bleachers at the Cariboo Memorial Recreation Complex was Ken Burgess who was proudly watching his daughters Olivia, 6, and Keanna, 12. “It’s great to have all the girls together on the ice at one time,” Burgess said, adding of the opportunity for the younger girls to learn how the older girls can play. Duff has more than 15 years of hockey coaching and teaching experience having gotten involved since his daughters wanted to play. This year he coaches the girls U15 Rep Team that includes players from Quesnel and 100 Mile House.

b61cd686a747dcf7c5a90b52fd84c12c.text: Cayenne, a 25-pound labradoodle, is now safe at home, unbothered by the whole ordeal. A Hollywood-esque search-and-rescue mission unfolded on the grounds of Victoria International Airport over the weekend, while most people were asleep. But this time, the target wasn’t an injured hiker or a lost adventurer, but a 25-pound labradoodle named Cayenne. Elizabeth Cage, Cayenne’s owner and operator of Duncan Doodles & Labradors, recounted the ordeal to the Peninsula News Review, which involved plenty of stress, a full-scale rescue operation by airport staff and, most importantly, a happy ending. It all began shortly after 9 p.m. on Oct. 24, election night, when a friend of Cage’s was supposed to deliver Cayenne to his uncle in Toronto. The uncle, who had recently lost his previous dog, was looking for a new companion. Hearing about this, Cage offered Cayenne, whom she believed would be a perfect fit. Shortly after arriving at the airport, Cage’s friend got out of the car, leashed Cayenne, and prepared his bags before the flight. However, the shy pooch managed to slip free from her collar and ran away after being spooked by a loud noise. With his departure imminent, Cage’s friend frantically searched for Cayenne in the long-term parking lot, but his efforts proved fruitless. With only minutes left before his flight, John called Cage to deliver the bad news. In a panic, Cage called her sister for reinforcements, and the two left Duncan in haste and arrived at the airport at around 10 p.m. In the rain, wind and darkness, the sisters began searching the area where Cayenne was last seen. That’s when Cage’s phone rang again. This time, it was the airport. “I got a phone call stating that she was sighted … on airport grounds,” Cage said. “So somehow, she got under a fence to get there. “We have no idea where or how she did it, and of course we can’t get in there to go get her.” With renewed hope, the sisters canvassed the surrounding area, from the nearby Rotary Park baseball

Dr. Hussein Hollands is urging the province to extend coverage to his patients for eye injection medication beyond Nov. 13, 2026. A number of patients in the North Okanagan could soon lose coverage for the eye injection medication that prevents them from going blind, leaving them to choose between onerous travel to receive the injections elsewhere or exorbitant bills to have them done locally. Vernon physician Dr. Hussein Hollands says that just two weeks from now, some of his elderly patients will be forced to choose a third option: going without the medication and suffering the consequences. Hollands, who specializes in medical retina ophthalmology, told The Morning Star that for months he’s been asking the Ministry of Health to accommodate his patients with extended coverage after he left a program he said was unfair to him. Coverage for eye injection medicine is currently tied to this program for retinal specialists in B.C., such that leaving the program effectively means cancelling the coverage. Hollands wants this to be changed. He is concerned that a number of his patients will soon be without the injections that are critical to maintaining their vision, unless the province heeds the call he’s been making to adjust its coverage model. The province is pinning the blame on Hollands for opting out of the program. But Hollands says the adjustment would be administratively straightforward and cost-neutral. He’s been asking the Ministry of Health for it since May and is unsure why he hasn’t been listened to. “Every day, I’ve been talking to patients who I know, after treating them for years with their retinal disease, that they will permanently lose their vision without this treatment,” Hollands said. “They cannot pay for this, and they cannot travel outside of the community, at least some of them, to get that treatment.” Hollands explained that these

57fba161d13fd2e09843059b83b4e1f7.text: The Quesnel River Rush played with the Quesnel Millionaires' jersey for Retro Night. **Thursday, Oct. 29 – Quesnel River Rush 3, Williams Lake Mustangs 11** The Quesnel River Rush watched a promising start unravel Thursday night as the Williams Lake Mustangs scored 10 goals over the final two periods in an 11-3 rout at the West Fraser Centre. On Thursday, Oct. 29, the River Rush opened the scoring exchanges with a strong start, keeping pace with Williams Lake through the first period. The Mustangs struck first when Kaelen Swanson scored at 2:31, but Quesnel responded just 26 seconds later as Luke Van Imschoot buried his ninth goal of the season on the power play at 2:57. The teams headed into the first intermission tied 1-1, with Quesnel showing early signs of being able to match the visiting Mustangs. Quesnel carried that momentum into the second period when Austin Root scored his first goal of the season at 3:24 to give the River Rush a 2-1 lead. However, Williams Lake quickly turned the game around. Kaden Charpentier tied the contest on the power play at 10:14 before Swanson scored twice in just over two minutes, including a power-play marker, to put the Mustangs ahead 4-2. Tristan Aidoo added another at 14:53, sending Williams Lake into the second intermission with a 5-2 advantage. The Mustangs continued to build their lead in the third period, with Logan Hauk scoring at 1:33. Quesnel’s Jimmy Proulx answered at 3:30 with his first goal of the season, briefly cutting into the deficit and making it 6-3. Williams Lake responded with five unanswered goals to close out the game. Braden Bolt scored at 4:30, followed by power-play goals from Chaz Lucas, Declan Pocock, Carter Krueger and Matthew Hufty as the Mustangs pulled away for the 11-3 victory. The Mustangs also controlled the shot count, outshooting Quesnel 54-31. Williams Lake recorded 28 shots in the third period alone, compared to just six for the River Rush. 785aebe67dff87e2f0e22bbc72c2412e.text: A South Cariboo man has been arrested for several charges, including committing violence towards an intimate partner. On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the 100 Mile House RCMP and the Cariboo Crime Reduction Unit executed a search warrant at a residence located along the 5400-block of Canim Hendrix Lake Road. The warrant was executed in relation to allegations of threats. They were supported by the North District Emergency Response Team. Cpl. Jennifer Cooper said that during this operation, a man associated with the residence was located and arrested a short distance from the home. Cooper identified him as 36-year-old Dylan Ryder Gropp. Gropp has been charged with the following four offences: conspiracy to commit an indictable offence; uttering threats to burn, destroy or damage; criminal harassment and committing a violent offence against an intimate partner. None of these charges has been proven in a court of law.
